accuracy.evidence: Checked against English Appendix 1 (Year 1 spelling): 'The prefix un- is added at the beginning of a word without any change to the spelling of the root word', with unhappy, undo, unload, unfair and unlock as the statutory examples. The two meanings (not, on adjectives such as unkind and unwell; reversal, on verbs such as unlock, untie, unzip, unpack) follow the Cambridge Grammar of the English Language account of un- prefixation. The non-prefixed words (under, uncle, unicorn) were checked: removing un leaves der, cle and icorn, none of which are English words.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text and seen in Year 1 spelling: putting un- after the word (step 1 back slot, challenge 'back' and 'end'), a gap (un happy, un kind; 'gap'), changing the root (unhapy, unzipp, undoo), writing on- (onzip, ondo; 'on'), reading un- as very or again ('very', 'again'), thinking unlock means keep it locked ('lockit'), and treating under, uncle and unicorn as un- words (step 4 and challenge 'under', 'uncle'). Step 5 includes a gap that needs the plain word kind, so un- is not chosen by habit.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagunpre is about this prefix's own mechanism: a front/back slot pair around the root, picture pairs where only the undone state (open lock, loose laces, open zip, empty bag) matches the un- verb, a take-off-un test that sorts unfair from under, and spelling tiles that keep the root intact. flagwordgap, flagnamecap, flagcmpd and flagplural share none of these; lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Every rule is met in action first: dragging un- to the back slot returns 'happyun is not a word. un- is a prefix, so it goes at the front: unhappy', the shut lock for unlock returns 'That one is still locked. unlock undoes lock, so it goes back the other way', and sorting under as un- returns 'Take off un and der is left. That is not a word'. Done screens list unkind = not kind and unlock: it undoes lock side by side, so both meanings are seen together.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong option: unhappy as 'very happy' (step 1 shows not happy), unzip as 'It shuts' (step 2 shows the open zip), and under as an un- word (step 4 shows der is not a word). The reveal line repeats the child's own choice when the task is finished.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages: very, again (re- not un-), on-spelling, gap, lock it, nothing happens, under, uncle, at the end, in the middle, the plain opposite happy, and happyun. Each names the slip and the fix, e.g. 'Take un off uncle and cle is left. That is not a word, so uncle has no prefix.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with one idea each (Put un in front of happy. Now you have unhappy. It means not happy.) and pass the validator's family readability limit. Canvas text is a single short line per round on 24-26 px word cards. The adult text uses the precise terms prefix, root word, adjective and verb with the statutory Appendix 1 wording.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases, and explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including Compound Words, Capitals for Names and Regular Plural Nouns. Each feedback line names the word and the reason; step texts are two or three sentences of instruction with no warm-up.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in light and a 360 px Android run in dark: the front and back slots sit either side of the root card with their labels below them, the four picture pairs fill two 170 px panels (after shrinking the unpacked bag so its items no longer touched the panel edge), sorting boxes sit side by side with the sorted words inside, and sentence gaps wrap above two 150 x 58 px choice cards.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed all five tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a labelled button ('Put un- in front of happy', 'unlock: the right picture', 'Spell it unhappy', 'unfair: un + a word', 'Fill the gap with untidy'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line. Word cards are dark ink on white or pale orange in both themes, with the un- part in dark brown (#7c2d12).
